patches.title: A rescue must be provable, attributable and atomic
patches.symptom: a split-out call could run under an empty or wrong tool name, replay without replayState, or commit before a later block of the same stream was rejected
patches.rootCause: block-end repairs committed as they arrived, one name per index, and stop emitted without replayState: the JSON proof held while the call could still be dispatched wrong

patches.title: A refusal must be observable, and a withdrawal must not read as a repair
patches.symptom: a stream whose only defect is plain bad JSON read "repair incomplete", and a withdrawn repair was indistinguishable from a fusion nobody could split
patches.rootCause: recordRejected incremented fused and unrepaired for every rejection whatever its code, so a refusal that never proved a fusion inflated fused — the difference between "we declined" and "we could not" was erased
limits: the four verdict states and their order are unchanged: the counts are reported, never judged
no state name can say "observed, refused, and correctly not repaired"; only the counter row carries it
old journal lines keep the six-field shape: no migration rewrites them

patches.title: A bare value after a member key must be resealed, or refused — never guessed
patches.symptom: a tool call fails with `Unexpected token` or `Unexpected end of JSON input` because the model wrote a program, not a JSON string, after `"code":`
patches.rootCause: a bare unquoted multi-line blob as one member value is neither a fusion nor splittable, so P-0001 refused it as `single-object` and the call never dispatched
limits: reseals only when exactly one member value proves; two possible resealings is refused as ambiguous
never touches a truncated call; a duplicate key, doubled colon, missing brace or illegal escape stays a refusal
keeps the call id: no synthetic identity, and the stream budget is untouched

patches.title: A second seam with no test is a seam nobody has ever run

patches.rootCause: the listener was written against an assumed contract: a handling listener returns {kind:"retry"} without calling next(), and a waterfall listener that does not own the decision must return next()
limits: only MALFORMED_RESPONSE is retried; SERVER, TRANSPORT and TIMEOUT self-heal upstream
the retry budget defaults to 0: nothing is retried unless a deployment asks for it
the bound is 256 cache entries; an evicted entry lets a very long turn spend a fresh retry
the live artifact is a synthetic endpoint: it reproduces the adapter failure, not a relay incident

patches.title: A resumed session can lose a tool it already called, and nothing counted it
patches.symptom: upstream #12348: a resume stops declaring a tool this session used and the host answers UNKNOWN_TOOL; nothing read a request/header here
patches.rootCause: scan read attempts, turns and codes, never request/header, so no rule compared a header with what the session had already called
limits: it proves the request set lost a tool the session used, not what the model remembers
a drop nobody called, and a call made only after the drop, are both refused
it counts resume and change alike, cannot see a provider that sends no header, and names no verdict

patches.title: explain had no word for the tool a resume dropped
patches.symptom: P-0050 counted lost tools in scan; explain printed turn endings only, so the shape #12348 reports stayed invisible where a decision is made
patches.rootCause: explain kept turns, codes and refused efforts from the scan report and dropped dropped_tools
limits: a finding, not a coverage row: coverage needs a resident seam
it names the request set moving, never what the model remembers; restoring it is out of scope
a session with no request/header is unmeasured, not clean

patches.title: A completed turn can end on the tool call the UI does not read
patches.symptom: upstream #12741: a long tool loop finishes `completed` on a step that still carries a tool call, and the UI shows only tool rows; scan counted the tool call as an answer (P-0044)
patches.rootCause: the host ends a step with tool calls only when a tool result carries `concludesTurn` (`dsh-agent-loop/src/agent.ts:592-603`), and ui-chat accepts only a final step with no tool-call block (`turn-process.ts:160-161`)
limits: a counter, not a repair: the host decides to conclude and the UI decides what is visible
counts completed only; a max_tokens turn on a tool call keeps P-0044 meaning
a finding, not a coverage row: no resident seam

patches.title: A chunk the wrapper cannot read became this plugin's exception
patches.symptom: a null chunk, a block-end whose arguments is not a string, a block-end with no block, or a finish with no reason ended the turn with a TypeError raised by remedy
patches.rootCause: the loop cast every yielded value and read type / block.type / block.arguments.trim() / reason.kind without a shape check, and the outer catch only recognised a proven fusion
limits: a fail-open stream reads quiet: the foreign chunk moves no counter
only the fields the wrapper reads are checked; an ignored field is not validated
a neighbour that returns its own stream or mutates chunks is outside this rule
a null chunk and a block-end with no block stay unattributable: the host reads the same field and fails the same way

patches.title: The fallback name was borrowed even when the profile already owned it
patches.symptom: a profile that declares remedy_unattributed received a repaired fragment under that name, and a nameless block-end was dispatched with it too
patches.rootCause: both dispatch sites (the foreign fragment in planRescue and the missing-name branch) wrote UNATTRIBUTED_NAME without asking whether options.tools already used it
limits: a rescue that might not have needed the fallback name is abandoned on purpose
it only sees the declarations the request carries; a later or hidden tool is invisible
the abandoned rescue is visible only as the provider error, with no counter of its own

patches.title: The reach metric called a window key "newest"
patches.symptom: the 2026-11-20 reach file named 0.4.19/0.4.18 as newest although 0.4.20 was published the day before, so two days of latest share compared different pairs of versions
patches.rootCause: latestShare sorted the npm download-window keys; a release published after the window closed has no row and was silently excluded, and the test imported the I/O script that could exit 2
limits: a share with missing versions is a lower bound, not comparable across days
the registry defines published; the download window defines rows, and the two can disagree
download counts are machine readings, not users
